title: CYBRIK soc.get_alert_context invocation transport-binding profile v1
description: Restriction-only transport-binding profile that carries the W1 C1 soc.get_alert_context business payload inside the existing W2-B tool-execution request/result/receipt envelope. Every envelope schema and the Fabric control-plane OpenAPI surface are reused byte-unchanged and this profile only narrows them: it adds no endpoint, path, operation, parameter, header, queue, MCP tool or capability-registry entry, and it defines no capability descriptor, signature envelope, executor isolation or network policy. Caller arguments are a closed set that cannot assert authorization_binding: Fabric completes the credential- and policy-derived binding after authorization and SOC returns it inside the business result. The capability descriptor digest stays an opaque value constrained only to exact equality across the envelope request, the completed business binding and the receipt. R0 dispatch is synchronous execute-only, so dry_run, queued and approval_required are out of profile; a fail-closed kill switch denies pre-dispatch with no business payload. Every C1 business outcome (available, unavailable, idempotency_conflict) is carried inside envelope status=completed as inline output.data with no artifacts. The receipt-signing envelope stays deferred and this profile invents none. Status: PROPOSED — NOT ACCEPTED; no endpoint, registry entry, Fabric invocation grant, runtime implementation, CI wiring or release claim.

boundCapabilityPin.description: Envelope-shaped capability pin narrowed to this one capability. digest stays an opaque registry-owned descriptor value: this profile neither defines nor decomposes it and constrains it only to exact equality across the envelope request, the completed business authorization binding and the receipt.

callerArguments.description: Closed capability-specific argument channel. It carries only the C1 business-request fields the accepted envelope has no slot for; idempotency_key, tenant_id, actor, purpose, capability and data_marking stay envelope-owned so no field has two competing wire homes. authorization_binding is deliberately absent: a caller may never assert the credential- and policy-derived binding, which Fabric completes after authorization and SOC returns inside the business result.

request_id.description: C1 business request id. It is a distinct namespace from the envelope action_id and must equal the business result request_id.

traceparent.description: Optional caller-asserted W3C trace context. Trace context is carried, never minted: the business result may omit traceparent, but any traceparent it does carry must equal this caller value exactly, so a result-side trace context can neither be fabricated when the caller asserted none nor drift from the one the caller asserted. That is a cross-document rule between the request and the result, so it is enforced by the packet validator rather than by this single-document schema.

idempotency_key.description: Narrowed to the accepted C1 business-request bound. The accepted W2-B envelope already requires minLength 16 and declares no ceiling, so this profile only adds the C1 maxLength: a bound request that the envelope would accept but that could not be reconstructed into a valid C1 business request is rejected at the transport layer instead of failing after dispatch.

purpose.description: Narrowed to the accepted C1 business-request bound. The accepted W2-B envelope already requires minLength 1 and declares no ceiling, so this profile only adds the C1 maxLength, keeping the envelope purpose and the reconstructed C1 purpose one value with one bound rather than two divergent ones.

execution.description: R0 dispatch is synchronous execute-only; dry_run is out of profile because a read capability has no side effect to simulate.

status.description: Synchronous R0 subset of the accepted envelope status set. queued is out of profile because dispatch is synchronous, and approval_required is out of profile because an R0 read is never approval-gated.

output.description: Inline business result channel. data is the accepted C1 business result document unchanged, so every C1 outcome — available, unavailable and idempotency_conflict — is carried inside envelope status=completed.

output_artifacts.description: The bounded R0 business result is always inline; no artifact locator channel is opened by this profile.

allOf.description: A completed dispatch of this capability must carry both receipt_id and the inline business output and may carry no error. This is a capability-scoped strengthening at the obligation layer only: the accepted W2-B tool-execution-result envelope leaves receipt_id optional for a completed result and this profile neither restates nor redefines that generic envelope rule — nothing here asserts that W2-B requires receipt_id for completed results in general. At the schema instance-set layer the profile stays strictly restriction-only, because promoting an already-permitted optional envelope field to required removes instances from the accepted envelope's set and adds none, so every document valid under this branch is also valid under the unmodified W2-B envelope.

error.description: A denial — including the fail-closed kill switch — is evaluated pre-dispatch, so nothing executed, no receipt exists and the denial is terminal.

allOf.description: Receipt profile for a dispatched R0 invocation. It requires the accepted receipt fields and adds none: the signing envelope stays deferred and `signature` remains the accepted opaque reference to it. Executor identity, isolation profile and network policy are left entirely to the accepted receipt contract.

status.description: A receipt exists only once dispatch happened. partial and rolled_back are impossible for a capability with no side effect, and pre-dispatch denial produces an envelope result with no receipt.
